title: Prior-summer water temperature did not predict next-year SAV area change in the Chesapeake Bay eelgrass zone or Maryland coastal bays in 1985-2025; a 1985-2015 heat model failed for 2016-2025
abstract: Question: do hot summers decrease the next-year area of submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) in Chesapeake Bay, mainly in the eelgrass (Zostera marina) zone, and does a model fitted on 1985-2015 predict 2016-2025? Data: VIMS aerial SAV survey (hectares per Chesapeake Bay Program segment, 1984-2025; 2025 preliminary), NOAA CO-OPS hourly water temperature at six stations (1994-2025), NOAA OISST v2.1 monthly SST, and USGS discharge of three rivers. Method: zone-level log change of SAV area from one year to the next, with only segments that VIMS mapped fully in both years; OLS with HC3 errors and permutation tests on July-August water temperature of the prior summer, spring flow and a density term; fit 1985-2015, test 2016-2025; tidal-fresh and oligohaline zones as placebos; Maryland and Virginia coastal bays as independent regions; a segment-level panel. Results: in the polyhaline (eelgrass) zone the heat slope was -0.003 +/- 0.068 log units per degree C in 1985-2015 (n = 29), -0.015 +/- 0.070 in 2016-2025 (n = 10) and +0.011 +/- 0.041 in 1985-2025; days at or above 28 C, raw OISST and the segment panel gave the same result. No model forecast 2016-2025 better than no change (skill -0.01 to -0.37). The area decreased by 40% and 36% after the 2005 and 2010 summers (+0.64 C), but increased by 35%, 5% and 20% after the hotter 2012, 2016 and 2020 summers (+1.2 to +1.5 C). The Maryland coastal bays gave no slope; the restored Virginia coastal bays gave a negative slope that was not robust. The oligohaline placebo segments gave a negative heat slope (-0.30 +/- 0.09), so heat-linked loss was not specific to eelgrass. OISST inside the bay agreed with in-situ year-to-year changes (r = 0.8) but warmed 0.9 C per decade against 0.3-0.5 in situ, with a level step near 2007 (about 3 C in mid-bay cells). Partial mapping changed oligohaline changes by up to 0.88 log units. Limitations: total SAV area is not eelgrass area, and widgeon grass can replace eelgrass after die-offs; the heat series is a regional summer mean; the test period has 10 changes; water clarity and nitrogen were not tested.
